- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.25) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) in recent days, model tends to underestimate; increase forecast slightly or allow upward bias.
- After a sharp spike in price, model often overshoots and fails to correct — apply a “cool-down” rule: reduce forecast by 5–10% after peak.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias — if price is above 30-day moving average, forecast should trend downward; if below, upward — adjust based on sentiment direction.
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to lagging sentiment shifts — if sentiment changes direction within 5 days, adjust forecast to reflect new sentiment trend early.
- When sentiment is volatile (e.g., alternating +/– 0.25), model tends to smooth too much — allow for 1–2% asymmetric adjustment toward sentiment direction.
